characters.name: Snow-White and Rose-Red
characters.description: A princess born as white as snow and as red as blood, who sets out to save her twelve brothers and endures years of silent work and false accusations without giving up.
characters.look: A slender young woman of about twenty with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder, tied with a strip of white linen. She wears a plain dark-teal homespun wool dress with a deep pocket, where the handle of a small silver spoon peeks out, a long grey wool shawl and thin, worn brown leather shoes.

characters.name: Snow-White and Rose-Red as Queen
characters.description: Snow-White and Rose-Red after she marries the young King. She sews on the shirts every day and cannot say a word, not even when the old Queen lies about her.
characters.look: A slender young queen of about twenty-four with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder under a slender silver circlet. She wears a long, plain gown of white linen embroidered with small red roses at the hem and cuffs, a deep-red girdle and soft grey leather slippers.

characters.name: The Queen
characters.description: Mother of the twelve princes and of Snow-White and Rose-Red. She wished for a daughter as white as snow and as red as blood, and gave away her sons to have her.
characters.look: A warm, motherly queen of about forty-five with a round face, a soft double chin, a small snub nose, kind hazel eyes, rosy cheeks and wavy chestnut hair going grey at the temples, pinned up under a small gold crown. She wears a long plum-purple wool cloak lined and trimmed with thick white fur over a plum gown, white fur mittens and fur-lined boots.

characters.name: The Troll-Wife
characters.description: A supernatural bargain-maker who promises the queen a daughter and claims the twelve sons once the child is christened.
characters.look: A short, stout old troll woman, no taller than a fence rail, with lumpy, sandy-beige skin like weathered sandstone, a huge knobbly nose shaped like a big potato, small beady black eyes, a wide crooked grin with three teeth and an enormous tangle of black-and-grey hair like a crow's nest, stuck with twigs and one black feather. A thin cow's tail with a tuft pokes out under her patched grey skirt, and she wears a ragged moss-green shawl and big grey felt boots.

characters.name: The Young King
characters.description: A hunting king who falls in love with the silent maiden, marries her, and is misled by blood and lies until the truth is spoken and the children are found alive.
characters.look: A tall, slim young king of about twenty-six, clean-shaven, with a long, friendly face, a straight nose, warm brown eyes, a wide smile and fair, straight hair tied back at the neck with a dark-blue ribbon, a thin gold circlet on his head. He wears a sky-blue wool coat trimmed with white braid, a broad brown leather belt, fawn breeches, soft grey leather boots and a short grey riding cloak.

characters.name: The Old Queen (Stepmother)
characters.description: The king’s jealous stepmother who frames the young queen by stealing her children and smearing blood, driving the court toward a wrongful burning.
characters.look: A bony, very upright old dowager queen with a long, pointed chin, a small hooked nose, narrow darting black eyes, thin lips and a chalk-pale face with two hard spots of rouge. Her steel-grey hair is piled high in a tall coil stuck with jewelled pins. She wears a stiff black wool gown shot with silver thread, a high collar of grey lace, rings on every finger and a small silver hand mirror on a chain at her waist.

characters.name: The Youngest Brother
characters.description: The youngest of the twelve princes, wild ducks by day and princes by night, who speaks up for his sister when the eldest wants her killed.
characters.look: A slim young man of about twenty-three, the smallest of twelve brothers, with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a faded bottle-green wool cap, a worn chestnut-brown wool tunic with a white linen collar and a rope belt, patched grey breeches and soft grey leather boots.

characters.name: The Youngest Brother with the Duck's Wing
characters.description: The youngest brother once the spell is broken. His shirt never got its left sleeve, so he has a duck's wing where his left arm should be.
characters.look: A slim young man of about twenty-six with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a new pure-white cap, shirt and kerchief of soft bog-cotton cloth, grey breeches and soft grey leather boots. In place of his left arm he has a large wild duck's wing of grey-brown feathers with a shiny blue-violet patch edged in white.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: A bright spring morning at the old royal manor, the birches in pale new leaf. The Queen, an old woman now with white hair, hurries down the steps with open arms to embrace the Maiden Queen. Beside them the Young King holds the baby girl, with two small boys with fair curls at his side, and behind them the Winged Brother and eleven more brothers in white lead their horses in through the gate. In the doorway waits her father, a thin old king with a short grey beard and a dark-green robe.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Queen: A warm, motherly queen of about forty-five with a round face, a soft double chin, a small snub nose, kind hazel eyes, rosy cheeks and wavy chestnut hair going grey at the temples, pinned up under a small gold crown. She wears a long plum-purple wool cloak lined and trimmed with thick white fur over a plum gown, white fur mittens and fur-lined boots.
- the Maiden Queen: A slender young queen of about twenty-four with snow-pale skin, rosy-red cheeks and lips, a soft oval face, a small straight nose and large dark-grey eyes with long black lashes. Her raven-black hair hangs in one thick, loose braid over her shoulder under a slender silver circlet. She wears a long, plain gown of white linen embroidered with small red roses at the hem and cuffs, a deep-red girdle and soft grey leather slippers.
- the Young King: A tall, slim young king of about twenty-six, clean-shaven, with a long, friendly face, a straight nose, warm brown eyes, a wide smile and fair, straight hair tied back at the neck with a dark-blue ribbon, a thin gold circlet on his head. He wears a sky-blue wool coat trimmed with white braid, a broad brown leather belt, fawn breeches, soft grey leather boots and a short grey riding cloak.
- the Winged Brother: A slim young man of about twenty-six with snow-pale skin, a narrow, gentle face, a small straight nose, large dark-grey eyes and tousled raven-black hair that sticks up at the back like ruffled feathers. He wears a new pure-white cap, shirt and kerchief of soft bog-cotton cloth, grey breeches and soft grey leather boots. In place of his left arm he has a large wild duck's wing of grey-brown feathers with a shiny blue-violet patch edged in white.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The royal manors are clusters of dark log buildings with turf roofs, carved gables and small leaded windows around a yard. The Queen's sleigh is small and red, drawn by two brown horses. The thirteen silver spoons are small and exactly alike. As wild ducks, the twelve brothers are mallard drakes with glossy bottle-green heads, white neck rings, chestnut breasts and grey backs. As men they look alike: pale, with tousled raven-black hair, bottle-green caps and chestnut-brown tunics; the eldest is the tallest and has a short black beard. Bog cotton grows in fluffy white tufts, and the caps, shirts and kerchiefs sewn from it are pure white. The snake pit is an old, dank walled stone yard behind the young King's manor. The three children are two small boys with fair curls and a baby girl with black hair.

This story's season, light and colours: One long tale through many seasons: a hushed white winter day of fresh snow under a low, pale sun at the start; mossy spruce-green forest and warm firelight in the brothers' cabin; the bog at sunrise, a sea of white bog cotton in thin mist and pale-gold light; cool grey stone and candlelight at the young King's manor; a smoky orange pyre glow under a slate-blue dusk; and a clear, fresh spring morning at the end. Accents of pure white, blood red and raven black.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
